claude delegate.live: Racy: the reference's provider commit batch (#39502) decides by timing whether a subagent's queued updates commit together: in 1 of 8 pinned local rounds it sent one more subagent.updated after the task's context-transfer.created than Rust. Matched in the other rounds.

claude delegate worktree.agent mcp: Racy: seen both matching and differing (8 pinned runs and the shards matched; a later shard run differed): the reference's task_status sometimes reads the task before its outbox finalizer records the result's context transfer, so its resultContextTransferId is null where Rust's is set, as in codex delegate's agent mcp.
claude delegate worktree.live: Racy: seen both matching and differing (1 of about 15 pinned local rounds differed): whether the child's completion records (subagent.updated, its node and turn item, the context transfer) land before or after the parent's next command starts depends on how fast each server runs the child in its worktree, which the fake CLIs' tool pacing does not fix.

claude delegate remote cancel.peer calls: Racy: seen both matching and differing: when its wait there ends, a server's follower reads the thread's reply only if the cancel has not recorded the task's result yet (the reference races the wait with the task's result, `raceFirst(endedHere)`), so either server may skip that one t3_thread_read.
claude delegate remote cancel.live: #39502 (ProviderCommitBatch) combines queued snapshots, as in claude delegate live: the reference sends the steered delivery's card once with its message, where Rust also sends its pending and completed updates (two more turn-item.updated notification); Rust starts the run that answers it after the first turn's checkpoint is captured, where the reference's starts just before. The items, messages, runs and the answer's run match.

claude delegate followup.live: Racy: the provider commit batch (#39502) decides by timing whether the first task's queued subagent updates commit together, and both sides vary: main's CI run 45294158798 saw the reference send one more subagent.updated after the task's context-transfer.created, and one of 8 pinned local rounds saw Rust send one more there. Matched in the other runs.
claude delegate followup.orchestration.subscribeThread (live turn: Racy: the reference's live turn sometimes does not settle before the harness stops waiting (the reference goes silent; Rust answers), seen both matching and differing, on main too.
claude delegate followup.agent mcp: Racy: in 1 of 8 pinned local rounds the reference's delivery turn did not settle before the harness stopped waiting (as its live turn sometimes does not, see the orchestration.subscribeThread entry), so its answer list lacks the turn's task_status. Matched in the other rounds.

claude delegate live.live: Racy: matched in 4 of 12 pinned local runs. Otherwise the reference steers the delegated result into the parent's running Claude turn (#39528) and queues the follow-up run while that turn still runs, sending the delivery's card once with its message and the queued run before the turn ends, where Rust also sends the card's pending and completed steer updates and creates the follow-up run after the turn ends. Which way it goes depends on whether the result arrives before the turn's last item.
claude delegate live.items: Racy: in 1 of 10 pinned local rounds Rust steered the delegated result into the parent's running Claude turn, so its notification item came before the turn's assistant message, where the reference queued it as the follow-up run after the turn. kiro turn.live: Racy: matched in 4 of 34 CI runs of this scenario (3 of 16 on main, before #362), and in none of 39 pinned local runs. Otherwise: Rust reports the provider thread's update just before the provider turn's start, where the reference's ACP adapter (in Kiro's flavor) reports it just after (Rust's turn records hang from the thread record, which the thread's update creates). And the reference's provider commit batch (#39502) takes Kiro's first snapshots together (its worker runs only once the ACP stream has handed over what it read), so it sends the assistant message items once, completed, where Rust, whose batch commits the first snapshot at once, also sends their running updates. The reference also reports the provider thread again for each of Kiro's `session_info_update`s (the user message id, the turn's start, completion and end, a permission's interaction), each with a new `updatedAt`, where Rust reports it again only when Kiro retitles its session.

antigravity auto-accept-edits read-only.items: Intentional difference from the reference (user decision: read-only commands shouldn't block Antigravity in auto-accept-edits). The command line `ls -la /workspace | wc -l` is on Rust's explicit allowlist of read-only commands, so Rust answers agy's permission request with allow_once at once, where the reference asks the user (who accepts here); both send agy the same reply. Rust's thread therefore has no approval_request item.

codex native subagent wake.live: After the parent's turn ended, the shared app-server holds what Codex sends about the child until the wake run's turn takes it, so Rust streams the subagent's progress, result and completion as that run starts, where the reference streams them as they arrive, before the wake; the reference also streams every update of the subagent, including those that change nothing, and the wake message's message.updated. The subagent's records and item, the child thread with its turn, the wake run with its notification and the thread's messages match the reference.

codex native subagent stop.live: The reference streams every update of the subagent, also those that change nothing (running again just before the interrupt's card), and the subagent node's interruption with the turn's end; Rust's stream is made of what changed in the thread, so it sends each change once and the node's status with the subagent's record. The parent's interrupted run and subagent, and the child thread with its interrupted command and turn, match the reference.

codex restart running.attempts: A restart of a running Codex turn runs in place on the reference: Codex can restart a turn with new input (supportsSteeringByInterruptRestart), so the run keeps going as its next attempt (reason steering_restart), its first attempt superseded and that attempt's root node interrupted, and the restart message joins the same run. Rust's runs have one attempt each, so it stops the run (interrupt items and a checkpoint) and runs the message as a run of its own, as it does for Claude.
